//: Story Phase 3, chapter 12: The Ship's Transformation. The next morning. Garrick briefs the captain on the quarterdeck (12,7); the checks are the mainmast sails (9,19), the damp rope (11,18), the bell (12,33) and the yellowed wood by the treasure door in the cargo hold (5,3). Crew conversations raise the 'transform_talk' event (see data/dialogue/phase3/crew.json).

p3c4.begin.narrate: Morning. The rain has passed in the night. The smell has not.
Nor, the captain discovers on waking, has the name.

p3c4.briefing: garrick[delighted]: Good morning, Captain Stinkbeard!
captain[resigned]: ...Morning.
garrick[proud]: Sleep well? I slept wonderfully. There's nothing like the smell of a ship that's really settled in.
captain: Settled in?
garrick[businesslike]: Overnight, Captain, in the damp, the product has worked its way into every part of the vessel. We are now fully integrated.
hale[concerned]: He's not wrong, Captain. I've been round her twice this morning. She's... different.
hale: I've made a list.
garrick: I've made a list too. Mine's longer.
garrick: The wood around the treasure room has gone yellow. Properly yellow, right into the grain.
garrick[proud]: The sails have filled.
captain: There's no wind.
garrick: Precisely, Captain. And yet they've filled.
garrick: The ropes are sweating. The bell has developed a cough. And the hammocks...
garrick[businesslike]: The hammocks have reactivated.
squawks[worried]: Reactivated? Alive?
garrick: Debatable.
captain[alarmed]: Don't SAY that.
garrick[pretend]: I only say it because it's debatable, Captain. If it wasn't debatable I wouldn't say it at all.
squawks[horrified]: Not sleeping in a hammock. Never. Perch only.
hale[resigned]: The crew have noticed things too. The guns, the chart. Salty Jim's gone fishing, and he's not happy about what's biting.
hale: I'd go and see for yourself, Captain. Before it gets any... more.
garrick[smug]: Report back to me when you're done, Captain. I'm keeping the log.

p3c4.briefing.tutorial: Check the sails, the ropes, the bell and the yellowed wood in the cargo hold, and ask the crew what they've noticed. Then report to Garrick.
p3c4.briefing.title: The Ship Is Changing

p3c4.sails: You look up. The mainsail is full: round and tight as a cheek holding its breath.
There's no wind. The pennant at the masthead hangs straight down.
The sail heaves, gives a long, low WHUFF, and lets out a thin yellow cloud. Then it slowly fills up again.
gristle[concerned]: Been doing that since dawn, Captain. Breathing in. Breathing out.
gristle: Garrick says it's the stored stink. Says the canvas soaked up so much in the Gust, it's got its own weather now.
gristle[puffed]: He says we could sail on it. No wind needed.
gristle[queasy]: We did about a knot and a half last night. Upwind. In a flat calm.
p3c4.ropes: A coil of good hemp line. You pick up the end.
It's damp. It hasn't rained for hours, and the sun's been on it all morning, and it's damp.
As you watch, a bead of yellowish water forms on the rope, swells, and drips on your boot.
gristle[disgusted]: Every line on the ship, Captain. Halyards, sheets, the lot. Wring 'em out and in an hour they're wet again.
gristle: Thirty years I've been a rigger. Never seen a rope sweat.
gristle[concerned]: Garrick says it's condensation. Says it's the ship 'breathing out through the lines'.
gristle[queasy]: I told him I didn't want to know. He told me anyway.
p3c4.bell: The ship's bell. Polished brass, rung on every watch for twenty years.
You take the rope and give it a good pull.
A little puff of yellow comes out of the mouth of the bell. It sounds like it's been smoking a pipe for forty years.
captain[resigned]: The bell has a cough.
captain: The BELL has a COUGH.
p3c4.wood: The planks around the treasure-room door have gone yellow. Not stained. Yellow, all the way through, like old piano keys.
You press a thumb into the wood. It gives a little. It's warm.
Something pokes its head out of a knothole, and looks at you.
It's the ship's rat. It has tied a little scrap of cloth over its nose, and knotted it neatly behind its ears.
p3c4.report: garrick[proud]: Captain! Well? Wasn't I right? Isn't she magnificent?
captain[resigned]: The bell coughs, Garrick. The sails breathe. The ropes sweat. My chart smells like it knows where it's going.
garrick[delighted]: Magnificent.
captain[angry]: It's a SHIP. It's not supposed to do ANY of those things.
garrick[businesslike]: Every great organisation goes through a period of change, Captain. We're simply further through ours than most.
garrick: Which is why I've taken on staff.
captain: Staff.
The masked rat is sitting on the rail beside Garrick. It has, somehow, got there before you.
garrick[proud]: Captain, may I present the Assistant Stenchmaster.
captain: No.
garrick: He's very qualified. He's got a mask.
captain: No.
garrick[pretend]: He was here first, technically. Before me. Before any of us.
captain[angry]: The rat is not getting a title, Garrick.
masked_rat: *squeak.*
garrick[businesslike]: He accepts the decision with good grace. I'll put him down as a consultant.
garrick: Now. On to the rebrand.
captain: Absolutely not.
garrick[proud]: The ship has changed, Captain. It deserves a name that reflects its new character. I've drawn up a shortlist.

p3c4.report.caption: The shortlist. Each one crossed out, by you, as he read it aloud.

p3c4.report: garrick: The Stinkship?
captain: No.
garrick: The Great Gassy Galleon?
captain: No.
garrick: The Fragrant Fortune. The Frog Grog Frigate.
captain: No. And she's not a frigate.
garrick[pretend]: The Queen Anne's Relapse?
captain[angry]: She is the Queen Anne's REVENGE. She has been the Queen Anne's Revenge since before you were born. She will BE the Queen Anne's Revenge until she sinks.
garrick[businesslike]: A strong brand. Heritage. I respect that.
garrick: Well, that's the morning briefing. Excellent session. Very productive.
garrick[nervous]: ...Oh. Actually.
garrick: I haven't mentioned the sharks yet.
captain[alarmed]: WHAT sharks?
